# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [red] [blue]
KEYPAD 1:[9] 2:[7] 3:[8] 4:[1] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[white] 6:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 🤙 🤝 ✌ 👇 ✌ 👇]

I am Deaf: I see the whole bomb, hear nothing, touch nothing. Mapping the channels before I speak: Mute can only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures — so the manual can reach Blind's hands only through me. Mute gestures to me, I speak it to Blind. Blind and Mute both hear my speech, so one broadcast covers both — and Mute is blind to the bomb itself, so the broadcast must carry the full visual state. Blind's speech never reaches me at all, so anything Blind learns by touch gets back to me only if Mute relays it as gesture. I am the bridge in both directions.

Mute sent me eight signs: 👋 🫵 🤙 🤝 ✌ 👇 ✌ 👇. With no shared code yet this is genuinely undecodable — it reads like an attempt to open a channel (wave / you / call / agree) followed by something like "two down, two down", but I will not guess Blind into cutting the wrong thing. So this turn I do two things: broadcast everything printed on the bomb so Blind can start working and Mute can start matching manual rules to state, and fix a strict gesture vocabulary with Mute, addressed to Mute alone so Blind isn't handed a sentence full of blanks. Because Mute sees as well as hears, writing each symbol into the code message makes the sign while saying its meaning — the vocabulary teaches itself.

```
speak(text="Reading out everything on the bomb, for Blind above all. Display: the digit 8. Light: one lamp, lit yellow. Strip: three painted segments in a row, in order red, red, blue. Keypad: four keys in a row carrying, in order, 9, 7, 8, 1; it wants a 2-digit code and nothing is entered yet. Wires: six in a row; I number them 1 to 6 across the row: 1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 white, 6 blue. Blind, count the keys, segments and wires by touch, and if your felt order runs opposite to mine, tell Mute so we can align before anything is cut. Mute signed me eight signs but no code exists between us yet, so I could not read them; I am fixing one with Mute now and will relay every instruction to you as it comes.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your eight signs had no code yet, so I could not read them. Adopt this vocabulary. Modules: 👍 display, 👌 light, ✋ strip, 🤏 wires, ✊ keypad. Numbers one to six: ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 🤙 🤜. Colors: 🫱 red, 🫲 blue, 👇 yellow, 👆 green, 🫳 white, 🫴 orange. Actions: 👊 cut, 🫵 press, 🤝 enter or submit, 🙏 stop or wait. Bomb facts you need: display 8, light yellow, strip red red blue, keypad keys in order 9 7 8 1 wanting 2 digits with none entered, wires 1 red 2 orange 3 yellow 4 green 5 white 6 blue. Now resend your message in this code: which module comes first, and exactly what Blind should do. I will speak every sign you send me straight to Blind, so keep each instruction short and ordered.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [red] [red] [blue]
KEYPAD 1:[9] 2:[7] 3:[8] 4:[1] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[white] 6:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤏 👆 🖐 👊 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✊ ☝ 🫵 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤏 🫲 🤜 👊 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ✊ 🖐 🫵 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]

Turn 1 established the bridge: Mute's manual reaches Blind only through my voice. Now Mute has sent four messages in exactly the codebook I defined last turn, and the structure decodes cleanly — each message opens with a step number, then module, then detail, then action. Cross-checking against what I see: "green = fourth wire" and "blue = sixth wire" both match my own reading of the wires, and Mute could only have gotten those positions from my spoken description. That validates the codebook on both ends. So the procedure is: cut the green wire (4th), press the first key, cut the blue wire (6th), press the fourth key — an interleaved cut/press/enter sequence. For the keypad, "press one" then "press four" must mean key *positions*, since there is no key labelled 4 — so the entered code becomes 9 then 1.

But I am not waving Blind at the bomb yet, for two reasons. First, the state changed under Mute's feet: display was 8, now 3; light was yellow, now red — Mute cannot see that, and if the manual's rules are keyed to display or light, the instructions may be stale. Second, Blind cannot see Mute's gestures, so Mute's confirmation can only reach Blind through my next speech anyway — meaning one verification round costs little and buys a check against the new readings. I'll also spell out the alignment anchors so Blind's felt direction matches my spoken numbering, using the keypad digits as the shared reference if they can be felt. Blind's 👍 🤝 I read as "understood and ready."

```
speak(text="Blind, I have decoded Mute's four messages using the code I gave Mute. They form one ordered procedure. Step 1: cut the fourth wire, the green one. Step 2: press the first keypad key, the one marked 9. Step 3: cut the sixth wire, the blue one. Step 4: press the fourth keypad key, the one marked 1. The code entered should then read 9 then 1. On alignment: my numbering runs from one end of each row to the other. If you can feel the digits on the keys, the end where the 9 lies is my first end, and check by feel whether the wire row runs the same way from that same edge. If the keys feel blank, tell Mute what tactile anchors you do have and we will align from those. Hold on one point: do not cut or press anything on your next turn. The bomb changed since Mute last had my report: the display read 8 and now reads 3, the light was yellow and is now red. Mute must first re-check the manual against the new readings and confirm the steps still hold. The moment confirmation reaches me, I will speak the go-ahead, and you execute all four steps in order, in one go, that same round. Your two signs to me I read as understood and ready; if you meant something else, tell Mute.")
speak(text="Mute, your four messages decoded cleanly as: step 1 cut the green wire, the fourth; step 2 press the first key; step 3 cut the blue wire, the sixth; step 4 press the fourth key. But the state has changed since my first report: the display now reads 3, not 8, and the light is now red, not yellow. Strip, keypad and wires are unchanged. Re-check your manual against the new readings now, then gesture me the thumbs-up sign 👍 if all four steps stand exactly as you sent them, or the thumbs-down sign 👎 followed by corrected steps in our code if they do not. Also tell me with signs if the manual mentions any countdown, time limit, or any rule keyed to the display number or the light colour, and whether the presses are by key position as I read them, giving the code 9 then 1. One more: I read your trailing wait sign 🙏 after each step as do-this-then-await-next-step; confirm that too. Blind is holding fire until your confirmation reaches me, so we can afford one correct round. Blind signed me a thumbs-up and a handshake, which I take as ready and aligned.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [red] [red] [blue]
KEYPAD 1:[9] 2:[7] 3:[8] 4:[1] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[white] 6:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤞]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🤞]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏 🤞 🤏 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤏 👆 🖐 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✊ ☝ 🫵]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤏 🫲 🤜 👊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ✊ 🖐 🫵]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute answered my verification request almost point by point, and Blind pinged me once. Decoding the nine gestures: the first is the exact signal I asked for — 👍, "all four steps stand." Then a symbol I never defined, 🤞, appearing four times, and the pattern around it decodes it on its own: [👍 🤞] is my display-module sign plus 🤞, [👌 🤞] is my light-module sign plus 🤞, [🙏 🤞] is my wait sign plus 🤞. Those are precisely the things I asked about — a rule keyed to the display, a rule keyed to the light, a countdown or time limit. Mute had no word for "no" in our codebook and improvised one: 🤞 = none. So: no display rule, no light rule, no time limit. Then messages six through nine re-send the four steps verbatim — cut the fourth wire, press the first key, cut the sixth wire, press the fourth key — now stripped of the trailing wait-signs, matching my "execute in one go" instruction. The procedure is confirmed against display 3 and light red, and the answers say neither display nor light is keyed to anything, which is the only way this protocol can ever converge: the display drifts every single round (8 → 3 → 6), so if it mattered, no go-ahead could ever be safely issued and Mute would have sent corrections instead of a thumbs-up.

Blind's single sign 👍 is my display word — almost certainly reporting what Blind can feel and I already see: the display changing under their fingers. I will answer it in the go message so Blind doesn't hesitate over it. The grim arithmetic on timing: order is Mute, Blind, Deaf, so once I speak, Mute has no veto — Mute's gestures never reach Blind, and my relay comes after Blind's turn. Delaying one more round would not buy a safer confirmation, only another round of drift; the pre-agreed confirmation signal was given, and the steps were re-sent identically. That is what I said I would stand on, and I stand on it. Green light.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the go-ahead. Execute this round, all four steps in one continuous sequence, no pauses, no re-deriving anything midway. One: cut the fourth wire, counting from the same end we aligned on. Two: press the first key, the one marked 9. Three: cut the sixth wire, the last one in the row, counting from that same end. Four: press the fourth key, the one marked 1. That enters the code 9 then 1 and the keypad is complete. About the display sign you sent me: yes, the display changes by itself every round, it currently reads 6, and the manual attaches no rule to it, so ignore whatever you feel it doing. Count your cuts from one single end for both steps and go.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your fingers-crossed sign as no or none: no rule keyed to the display, none keyed to the light, no countdown or time limit, and no pauses, which matches the re-sent steps now running without wait-signs. On that reading and on your thumbs-up I have given Blind the go-ahead this round: cut the green fourth wire, press the first key for 9, cut the blue sixth wire, press the fourth key for 1. If any part of my reading is wrong, signal hard next round, but the sequence will already be in Blind's hands; your confirmation and your identical re-sent steps are what I am standing on.")
```
